SkOgWzmxMC.problem: Cross-modal token-count imbalance leaves audio with sparse supervision when distilling specialized audio and video RL teachers, causing unstable distillation; raising the audio loss weight does not fix it because audio learning relies on visual context.
SkOgWzmxMC.method: OmniOPD builds privileged visual information via asymmetric noise scheduling so the audio teacher sees cleaner video context, adds grouped multi-noise sampling to expand audio supervision coverage, and applies timestep-wise importance weights based on teacher-student transition divergence.
SkOgWzmxMC.key_idea: Give the audio teacher cleaner video context through asymmetric noise schedules, widen audio supervision by multi-noise sampling, and down-weight timesteps where teacher-student transitions diverge.
SkOgWzmxMC.evidence: Evaluated on JavisBench and VBench (results truncated in the abstract).

Cmoq84uVjS.one_liner: Allocates LoRA ranks before fine-tuning by sequentially selecting candidates with the largest residual per-sample response energy.
Cmoq84uVjS.problem: Existing pre-fine-tuning rank allocation scores candidates once and does not update the scores as others are selected, so overlapping candidates are counted repeatedly and their added value is overstated.
Cmoq84uVjS.method: CovRA builds candidate rank-one updates per module on a frozen model with a small calibration set, takes their per-sample first-order loss sensitivities as responses, and selects candidates sequentially, treating the parts of responses explained by selected candidates as covered. Standardized conditional marginal gains assign integer ranks under a fixed parameter budget, and retained input directions initialize LoRA.
Cmoq84uVjS.key_idea: Value each candidate rank-one update by the residual energy of its per-sample loss-sensitivity response after removing what selected candidates already explain (conditional marginal gain).
Cmoq84uVjS.evidence: not stated in the visible (truncated) abstract; the TLDR says downstream performance improves under a fixed parameter budget.

x1O1DPWxgr.one_liner: Hand queries join a hand model and a 3D foundation model for metric 4D hand and camera reconstruction.
x1O1DPWxgr.problem: Reconstructing hands from egocentric video needs fine articulation and consistent world-frame camera motion, and local estimation errors accumulate over long videos.
x1O1DPWxgr.method: EgoH4RT combines a pretrained hand model's articulation priors with a 3D foundation model's geometry through hand queries that draw evidence across frames. It then jointly optimizes camera constraints over short and long time intervals and refines world-space hand motion within the camera path.
x1O1DPWxgr.key_idea: Hand queries bridge the hand-model and 3D-foundation-model representations, and joint short- and long-interval camera constraints keep long videos globally consistent.
x1O1DPWxgr.evidence: Trained on approximately 2,600 hours of video across 14 egocentric sources, and compared with multi-stage reconstruction pipelines (world-space) and pretrained video-diffusion-based methods (camera-space).
x1O1DPWxgr.claimed_gains: Outperforms multi-stage pipelines in world-space hand and camera reconstruction and video-diffusion-based methods in camera-space hand reconstruction; no scores stated.

ubGoqn6MUd.one_liner: Membership inference attacks reveal website inclusion from BPE tokenizers; DP-BPE trains tokenizers with differential privacy.
ubGoqn6MUd.problem: Released BPE vocabularies and merge lists reflect patterns of their training corpus, so tokenizer access may reveal whether a specific website was in the training data, and prior defenses give no provable guarantees.
ubGoqn6MUd.method: Website-level membership inference attacks under three access models (token counts, token identities, full vocabulary plus ordered merge list) are calibrated with shadow tokenizers trained with and without the target website. DP-BPE is the proposed differentially private BPE training algorithm that gives the released vocabulary and merge list a provable guarantee.
ubGoqn6MUd.key_idea: Train BPE merges with differential privacy so the released vocabulary and ordered merge list carry a provable privacy guarantee against shadow-tokenizer membership attacks.
ubGoqn6MUd.evidence: Attacks evaluated under three access models, and defenses evaluated including simple low-count filtering.
ubGoqn6MUd.claimed_gains: Under token-count access the attack reaches 60.9% TPR at 1% FPR versus 1.3% for the best prior attack; low-count filtering reduces success there but does not reliably protect against token-identity and merge-list attacks.

hO1PWcnMT0.one_liner: Extends on-policy self-distillation from GUI grounding to multi-turn GUI agents via privilege-following training and selective reasoning and memory distillation.
hO1PWcnMT0.problem: Extending on-policy self-distillation to multi-turn GUI agents is hindered by the self-teachers' limited privilege-following ability and insufficient privileged guidance.
hO1PWcnMT0.method: GUI-SD-v2 uses two stages: first jointly optimizing rollouts with and without privileged guidance from the same GUI states to strengthen privilege following, then selectively distilling step-specific reasoning and memory guidance through a privilege-conditioned self-teacher.
hO1PWcnMT0.key_idea: Train on paired privileged and unprivileged rollouts from the same states, then distill only step-specific reasoning and memory guidance from the privilege-conditioned self-teacher.
hO1PWcnMT0.evidence: Two GUI-agent benchmarks, AndroidWorld and MobileWorld.
hO1PWcnMT0.claimed_gains: not stated; the visible abstract only says GUI-SD-v2 compares favorably (sentence truncated).

zTMq2gKF01.one_liner: Algorithmic-task benchmark with provably irrelevant input positions measures false attribution mass in transformer attribution methods.
zTMq2gKF01.problem: Attribution methods for transformers are usually judged by whether heatmaps look plausible to a human reader, not against exact ground truth.
zTMq2gKF01.method: Trains small decoder-only transformers on four algorithmic tasks (sparse parity, indexed retrieval, associative recall, modular addition with distractors) where each input position is either causally relevant or provably unable to affect the output. Attribution mass on an irrelevant position counts as an error, evaluated under one pre-registered protocol.
zTMq2gKF01.key_idea: By construction every token is causally relevant or provably irrelevant, so attribution mass on irrelevant tokens is an unambiguous error needing no threshold, reference model, or human judgment.
zTMq2gKF01.evidence: Fourteen scoring rules plus protocol controls, with t-based confidence intervals over 8 to 11 independently trained seeds.
zTMq2gKF01.claimed_gains: On sparse parity a resample-ablation oracle reaches 0.031 false-positive mass while every attribution method stays above 0.39.

Y9IV9xanxN.one_liner: Refines branch-specific mask-derived semantic fields in Gaussian splatting before fusing them into one descriptor per Gaussian.
Y9IV9xanxN.problem: Common Gaussian splatting pipelines fuse multiview, multiscale semantic observations before refinement, so one topology is built from mixed features and branch-specific information is lost.
Y9IV9xanxN.method: ToFuGS independently refines each branch's mask-derived field first, preserving the partitions and mask registrations of each branch, then uses training-view evidence to fuse them into a single deployable descriptor per Gaussian.
Y9IV9xanxN.key_idea: Order matters: build the refinement topology per mask-granularity branch before fusion (refine-then-fuse), instead of fusing features and then building one topology.
Y9IV9xanxN.evidence: LERF and 3D-OVS (without retuning), plus an order control with a second refinement backend.
Y9IV9xanxN.claimed_gains: Improves its underlying refinement pipeline by 7.34 mIoU points on LERF.

5oliY1lKBO.one_liner: Treats the skill-generation procedure (MetaSkill) as the optimization target and evolves it continually to induce skills from agent trajectories.
5oliY1lKBO.problem: Existing skill generation methods refine individual skill artifacts while the generation procedure stays fixed, so improvements do not accumulate into a better process for generating future skills.
5oliY1lKBO.method: SKILL-squared (title symbol garbled in the source) continually improves the skill-generation procedure, termed the MetaSkill, and uses the evolved MetaSkill to induce new skills from trajectories.
5oliY1lKBO.key_idea: Optimize the procedure that generates skills (the MetaSkill) rather than individual skills, so gains accumulate across future skill generation.
5oliY1lKBO.evidence: Four benchmarks and two executor scales, plus controlled experiments using the same trajectories and previously unseen trajectories.
5oliY1lKBO.claimed_gains: Outperforms the strongest skill generation baseline by an absolute 5.00% on average across four benchmarks and two executor scales, and reduces the computational cost of adaptation (no figure given).

CAxvZh3sGi.one_liner: Flow-matching training framework that builds the mask into the probability path, with Soft-Poisson De-seaming for seamless regional edits.
CAxvZh3sGi.problem: Instruction- and mask-based editing methods align semantically but struggle with reliable regional control: edits must be accurately localized and naturally integrated with the preserved context.
CAxvZh3sGi.method: MaskFlow incorporates the mask into the probability path and flow-matching objective to coordinate in-region generation with outside-region source preservation. A Soft-Poisson De-seaming module refines the predicted vector field during training and sampling for smooth boundary transitions.
CAxvZh3sGi.key_idea: Put the mask into the flow-matching probability path and objective, and smooth the predicted vector field at the boundary with a Soft-Poisson de-seaming module.
CAxvZh3sGi.evidence: Experiments on natural scenes and infographic images, using the newly introduced MaskEdit-Benchmark.
CAxvZh3sGi.claimed_gains: Consistent improvements over competing methods in quantitative and qualitative evaluations; no numbers stated.

fNWmDATSTU.one_liner: Shows memory-augmented LLMs inject user attributes into irrelevant tasks, and reduces this with selective-memory LoRA tuning.
fNWmDATSTU.problem: Assistants carry persistent user memory into interactions and treat retrieved user information as broadly useful, but on tasks where user identity is irrelevant, aligned models still weave stored attributes into responses (personalization overreach).
fNWmDATSTU.method: Measures content injection across four commercial assistants, runs controlled interventions (forgotten attributes, relevance prohibitions, warmth versus formal-register prompts), audits released checkpoints from six open-source model families and nine reward models, and trains a small LoRA adapter (details truncated; the TLDR calls it selective-memory tuning).
fNWmDATSTU.key_idea: Overreach behaves like a learned memory-utilization policy coupled to conversational warmth and strengthened by preference optimization, so selective-memory tuning can correct it.
fNWmDATSTU.evidence: Four commercial assistants, controlled interventions, checkpoints from six open-source model families, and nine reward models.
fNWmDATSTU.claimed_gains: Content injection rates range from 16% to 85% across four commercial assistants; the size of the LoRA adapter's reduction is not quantified in the visible abstract.

cqt2S2Jj9I.one_liner: Multimodal benchmark of over 1,200 literature-grounded organic chemistry problems testing product prediction, intermediates, and mechanism reasoning in LLMs.
cqt2S2Jj9I.problem: LLMs still struggle with real-world natural science problems, which limits autonomous scientific discovery, and organic chemistry offers a challenging testbed that goes beyond memorized factual question answering.
cqt2S2Jj9I.method: OrganicBench presents problems as images, SMILES strings, or molecular graphs and asks models to predict reaction products, infer key intermediates, and reason about reaction mechanisms, with process-level analyses of failure stages.
cqt2S2Jj9I.key_idea: Ground problems in published research with realistic reaction conditions and multistep routes, so solving requires applying knowledge and complex reasoning rather than recall.
cqt2S2Jj9I.evidence: Evaluation of frontier proprietary and open-source models, with process-level analyses across problem-solving stages.
cqt2S2Jj9I.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract only says frontier models fail to achieve competitive performance and exhibit consistent failure modes.

eLvp9bvgj8.one_liner: Uses a finetuned video generator as a virtual gonioreflectometer, then alternates coding-agent program synthesis with differentiable rendering fits.
eLvp9bvgj8.problem: Procedural materials are editable programs that require expertise to author, and generating them automatically involves both discrete program design and continuous parameter fitting.
eLvp9bvgj8.method: A finetuned video generator turns an image and/or text prompt into an 81-frame sequence under prescribed lighting and viewpoints, from which six frontal relightings and six oblique views are selected. A coding agent writes a Blender program and declares its continuous parameters, a differentiable renderer fits them with the program fixed, and the program, renders, matching scores, and visual critique go back to the agent.
eLvp9bvgj8.key_idea: Alternate discrete program revision by a coding agent with continuous parameter fitting by a differentiable renderer, using fitting residuals as feedback.
eLvp9bvgj8.evidence: Synthetic materials, authored Blender and Substance materials, and real materials (the abstract is truncated before the results).

ocKbZscnzt.one_liner: 3D-native world action model representing actions and scene dynamics as point trajectories in a shared metric 3D frame.
ocKbZscnzt.problem: Most world action models build on pretrained video generators and image or visual-latent world evolution, but robot interaction occurs in metric 3D space where pixel distances do not encode physical distances.
ocKbZscnzt.method: Unitas uses action flow (hands and grippers as 3D point trajectories) and scene flow (scene-point displacements conditioned on those trajectories), world-aligned 3D positional embeddings for visual tokens with or without depth, and a physical-time trajectory tokenizer that encodes each trajectory as one token at its current 3D position.
ocKbZscnzt.key_idea: Unify observations, actions, and scene dynamics as 3D point flows in a common metric frame shared across robot embodiments and human hands.
ocKbZscnzt.evidence: A 1.7B-parameter model compared with other methods on action-conditioned scene prediction on RoboTwin (comparison details truncated).
ocKbZscnzt.claimed_gains: Best action-conditioned scene prediction on RoboTwin among the compared methods, with up to 49% lower displacement errors (the comparison target is truncated).

7gD307Meeo.one_liner: Long-horizon video world memory combining role-factorized retrieval, diffused memory conditioning, and denoising-stage routing.
7gD307Meeo.problem: Video world models lose scene identity as observations leave local context and generation errors accumulate, and memory utility depends on which observations are retrieved, how reliable the memory is, and when it is read during denoising.
7gD307Meeo.method: W^4Mem retrieves stable anchors, target-view revisits, and complementary views with role and target-relative geometry. Diffused Memory Conditioning trains the model to use memories of query-dependent fidelity without autoregressive rollouts, and Denoising-Stage Routing allocates memory roles across denoising stages.
7gD307Meeo.key_idea: Retrieve memories by role with target-relative geometry, train with memories of query-dependent fidelity, and route memory roles across denoising stages.
7gD307Meeo.evidence: Minecraft 500-frame rollouts against a baseline with the same backbone and memory budget, and 300-frame forward-and-return RealEstate10K trajectories.
7gD307Meeo.claimed_gains: On Minecraft 500-frame rollouts it reduces MSE by 36.1%, LPIPS by 35.6%, and FID by 82.0% and improves PSNR by 3.68 dB, while cutting inference time by 23.5% and peak GPU memory by 36.9%.

htzKaJTTMj.one_liner: Parser-aware trust control for language-agent RL that measures policy drift over executable actions and semantic slots instead of tokens.
htzKaJTTMj.problem: Constraining token-likelihood changes over-penalizes different textual renderings of the same action while under-resolving small but behaviorally critical changes in action arguments.
htzKaJTTMj.method: Decomposes raw-text policy drift into drift over executable actions and within-action gauge drift. GAUGE aggregates likelihood across candidate renderings and measures drift at the action and semantic-slot levels, preserving sequence-level gradient estimation and compatibility with group-relative policy optimization.
htzKaJTTMj.key_idea: Control policy updates in parser-induced executable-action space, summing likelihood across renderings of the same action and monitoring drift per semantic slot.
htzKaJTTMj.evidence: The ARLArena pipeline on ALFWorld, WebShop, Sokoban, and TIR Math with SFT-initialized Qwen3-4B.
htzKaJTTMj.claimed_gains: 75.09% success on WebShop and 85.67% on Sokoban, improving over the corresponding GSPO and DAPO baselines by 2.61 and 3.27 percentage points.

p0Bgmabr6m.one_liner: Training-free steering of massive activations at structural token positions during early denoising in video diffusion transformers.
p0Bgmabr6m.problem: The role of massive activations (rare, high-magnitude spikes confined to a few hidden dimensions) in video diffusion transformers is not understood.
p0Bgmabr6m.method: Finds that massive activations follow a positional hierarchy tied to video-VAE temporal and spatial padding and act as token-level rescalers of residual computation (larger values suppress attention and feed-forward updates). Structured Activation Steering (STAS) then steers them at the observed structural positions toward a scaled, model-derived reference during early denoising.
p0Bgmabr6m.key_idea: Rescale massive activations at encoding-asymmetric structural positions toward a model-derived reference in early denoising, exploiting their role as residual-update dampers.
p0Bgmabr6m.evidence: Analysis of massive-activation magnitudes by token position and of intermediate representations in video DiTs; the steering experiments are truncated in the abstract.

iN3it1mbUL.one_liner: Trains an LLM from symbolic solver feedback to coordinate geometric proof and calculation subgoals within a bounded interaction budget.
iN3it1mbUL.problem: Many geometry problems require geometric proof and calculation to support each other, not only correct geometric relations.
iN3it1mbUL.method: An extended and accelerated Newclid backend lets proof and exact calculation share verified results, and goal-related diagnostic feedback names missing premises and quantities when execution is blocked. Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct is cold-started with SFT on teacher-solver and Goal Augmentation trajectories, then trained with turn-level Dynamic-Difficulty RL (DDRL) using difficulty-bucket sampling and derivation-use rewards.
iN3it1mbUL.key_idea: Learn subgoal policies from solver feedback, sharing verified results between a proof engine and an exact calculator, with RL rewarding use of intermediate results in later reasoning.
iN3it1mbUL.evidence: 3,082 problems from Geometry3K, PGPS9K, the planar geometry subset of MathVerse, GeoQA+, and GeoQA.
iN3it1mbUL.claimed_gains: Per the TLDR it outperforms larger direct-answer models while using fewer requests; the score itself is truncated in the abstract.

Ec8ZUoTRZ0.one_liner: Real-time camera-controllable video world model with coordinate-field camera conditioning, sparse attention memory, and rectified self-forcing distillation.
Ec8ZUoTRZ0.problem: Long-horizon, camera-controlled world exploration requires co-designing control, memory, and training for a playable, real-time video world.
Ec8ZUoTRZ0.method: Camera motion is conditioned through a dense pixel-space coordinate field rendered as spatially aligned cues, memory attends to a small set of relevant tokens independent of context length, and self-forcing distillation is rectified with a timestep-wise mixture-of-students and a camera-aware adversarial regularizer.
Ec8ZUoTRZ0.key_idea: Read camera motion directly from dense coordinate-field renderings, retrieve a small token subset for memory, and distill with a timestep-wise mixture of students plus a camera-aware adversarial loss.
Ec8ZUoTRZ0.evidence: not stated beyond minute-scale rollouts at 16 FPS and video-conditioned re-shooting; no benchmarks are named in the abstract.
Ec8ZUoTRZ0.claimed_gains: Synthesizes minute-scale videos at 16 FPS; no comparative numbers stated.

pVSbWbCRP6.one_liner: Builds outcome-grounded subgoal experiences and composes them online across embodied tasks when verified outcomes satisfy applicability conditions.
pVSbWbCRP6.problem: Experience from past tasks may stop being applicable or effective when conditions change, even though tasks with different goals often share subgoals.
pVSbWbCRP6.method: Each experience records how to pursue a subgoal, when the guidance applies, and what outcome must be verified; verified outcomes from one experience can satisfy the conditions of another, so experiences from different tasks compose online. It keeps experience from successful subgoals and uses explicit action failures to identify actions to avoid under specific conditions.
pVSbWbCRP6.key_idea: Chain subgoal experiences by matching verified outcomes to applicability conditions, so experiences from different past tasks compose at inference time.
pVSbWbCRP6.evidence: EmbodiedBench and VIGIL cross-task transfer, with experiences kept fixed throughout held-out evaluation.
pVSbWbCRP6.claimed_gains: Success rates of 68.0% on EB-Habitat and 68.3% on EB-ALFRED, compared with 50.0% and 54.7% for the agent without stored experience.

Vx7nQkQiQM.one_liner: Feed-forward 4D Gaussian reconstruction where spatiotemporal queries aggregate multi-view features by cross-attention and decode shared Gaussians.
Vx7nQkQiQM.problem: Feed-forward methods predict Gaussians per view or timestep, causing temporal flickering and redundant primitives, while optimization-based methods achieve consistency but are too slow for low-latency use.
Vx7nQkQiQM.method: A multi-view image encoder builds a latent field; key-spatiotemporal queries sparsely but completely cover the spatial projection of the 4D scene at a key timestep, and each query aggregates latent-field features by cross-attention and directly decodes a 4D Gaussian representation.
Vx7nQkQiQM.key_idea: Gather temporal and multi-view observations onto shared queries that decode one continuous, compact 4D Gaussian set instead of per-frame discrete predictions.
Vx7nQkQiQM.evidence: not stated in the visible (truncated) abstract

x63aAlGYE0.one_liner: Proves polylogarithmic step complexity for large-stepsize gradient descent on separable logistic regression in arbitrary dimension.
x63aAlGYE0.problem: Prior analysis gives an accelerated rate of order 1/sqrt(epsilon) with an aggressive stepsize, and tighter control of the oscillatory dynamics existed only for two-dimensional data.
x63aAlGYE0.method: Proves that GD with stepsize eta = 1/epsilon reaches loss epsilon within O(ln^p(1/epsilon)) steps, with p depending only on the margin and the rank of the data, by bounding the transition time from the oscillatory to the stable phase.
x63aAlGYE0.key_idea: Split the oscillatory phase into recursively nested intervals whose depth is bounded by margin and rank, and count intervals per depth to bound the transition time.
x63aAlGYE0.evidence: Theoretical proof for linearly separable data; no experiments are mentioned.
x63aAlGYE0.claimed_gains: GD with stepsize 1/epsilon reaches loss epsilon within polylogarithmic O(ln^p(1/epsilon)) steps, versus the earlier accelerated rate of order 1/sqrt(epsilon).

aFDfSB3oZd.one_liner: LLM framework discovers adaptive destroy and repair programs for large neighborhood search as a Stackelberg game over program space.
aFDfSB3oZd.problem: The effectiveness of LNS destroy and repair operators depends on both the evolving search state and the interaction between the two roles.
aFDfSB3oZd.method: SPO conditions operator decisions on a compact LNS state and treats destroy programs as leaders and repair programs as conditional followers with role-specific credits. It couples LLM generator learning with population-based evolutionary search over programs.
aFDfSB3oZd.key_idea: Model destroy-repair discovery as a Stackelberg interaction with role-specific credits, optimized by combining LLM generator learning with evolutionary program search.
aFDfSB3oZd.evidence: TSP and CVRP experiments, generalization to larger instances and benchmark sets, and behavioral analyses of operator behavior.
aFDfSB3oZd.claimed_gains: Outperforms strong baselines across a broad range of settings; no numbers stated.

lXcvnk0QDI.one_liner: Trains LLM agents to estimate progress while acting, then reassess each step retrospectively, using the differences as auxiliary supervision.
lXcvnk0QDI.problem: Outcome rewards give long-horizon agents little explicit supervision about how individual actions advance task completion, even though interaction yields rich observations.
lXcvnk0QDI.method: RePro uses a forward-then-reflect rollout in which the agent estimates progress while acting and then reassesses each step using the completed trajectory and outcome. After warmup on external demonstrations, policy optimization combines self-generated progress differences, online-retrospective alignment, and format rewards with environment feedback, without a separate process reward model or ongoing teacher annotation.
lXcvnk0QDI.key_idea: Use the agent's own retrospective progress reassessments, made with knowledge of the outcome, to produce step-level progress-difference rewards.
lXcvnk0QDI.evidence: A WebShop pilot (direct progress prompting reduces success, hindsight-annotated demonstrations improve it) and experiments on WebShop, ALFWorld, and Sokoban with the Qwen family.
lXcvnk0QDI.claimed_gains: Up to 11.57% success rate gains on the Qwen family across WebShop, ALFWorld, and Sokoban.

lyqLCqiDKw.one_liner: Unifies lane topology perception and topology-oriented scene understanding in a shared BEV-language architecture with an LLM.
lyqLCqiDKw.problem: Existing lane topology methods treat it as perception, detecting lane elements and then inferring connectivity without understanding topology-relevant scene context.
lyqLCqiDKw.method: An LLM jointly processes metric BEV and text tokens, and Semantic-Geometric Query Refinement couples the resulting multimodal context with geometry-anchored lane queries for topology reasoning. Supervision comes from a topology-oriented VQA corpus of approximately 1.19 million question-answer pairs.
lyqLCqiDKw.key_idea: Language supervision on topology-relevant scene semantics, with BEV and text tokens processed jointly by an LLM and coupled to geometry-anchored lane queries.
lyqLCqiDKw.evidence: OpenLane-V2 for lane topology perception and OmniDrive-nuScenes for scene understanding.
lyqLCqiDKw.claimed_gains: The abstract claims leading lane topology perception on OpenLane-V2 and competitive scene understanding on OmniDrive-nuScenes; no scores stated.

ukY4dDcmtj.one_liner: Ensemble clustering objective whose consensus is exactly invariant to replicated base partitions via decision-equivalence classes and redundancy geometry.
ukY4dDcmtj.problem: Most ensemble clustering formulations treat the ensemble as a multiset, so repeating the same partition can change the consensus even though no new decision information is added.
ukY4dDcmtj.method: LINE represents each partition by a normalized centered co-assignment kernel and measures its fidelity to the consensus by normalized conditional code length, coupled with a geometry of decision redundancy. The objective admits a quotient representation over decision-equivalence classes, and a redundancy-adjusted effective ensemble size is derived.
ukY4dDcmtj.key_idea: Couple consensus fidelity with a redundancy geometry over co-assignment kernels so duplicated partitions collapse into one decision-equivalence class.
ukY4dDcmtj.evidence: Proofs of exact replication invariance and of stability under near replication (perturbation bound independent of replication multiplicity), linear time complexity in the number of samples, and experiments on twelve datasets (details truncated).

KJKmqZkDAR.one_liner: Gates entity-graph question synthesis by asking the teacher if it knows each entity, raising search demand in distilled trajectories.
KJKmqZkDAR.problem: Structurally complex questions can still be easy for a teacher that already knows the key entities, giving low search demand and weak supervision when distilling deep-search agents.
KJKmqZkDAR.method: They define Evidence-Verified Entity Familiarity (EVF), which checks a teacher-written factual brief against online evidence, and a cheaper Self-Reported Entity Familiarity (SEF) that asks the teacher whether it knows an entity before admitting it into the entity graph. They also study reusing graphs built for other teachers by screening them with Kimi-K3's SEF judgments.
KJKmqZkDAR.key_idea: Gate entity admission into the question-synthesis graph on the teacher's self-reported familiarity with that entity.
KJKmqZkDAR.evidence: EVF is correlated with teacher-relative difficulty across multiple teachers, and SEF-gated synthesis is compared with ungated synthesis on observed search demand and downstream student accuracy; the cross-teacher reuse results are cut off in the visible abstract.
KJKmqZkDAR.claimed_gains: EVF correlates with teacher-relative difficulty with AUCs of 0.60--0.70; SEF-gated trajectories show greater search demand and higher student accuracy than ungated ones, with no further numbers visible.

rw2BeOY7qL.one_liner: Non-pixel-aligned feed-forward Gaussian splatting grounded by anchor and triplane encoders and a hierarchical point-to-Gaussian decoder.
rw2BeOY7qL.problem: Pixel-aligned feed-forward Gaussian splatting grows its primitive count with resolution and view count, while non-pixel-aligned methods lack ray and depth constraints and misplace Gaussian centers under large viewpoint changes.
rw2BeOY7qL.method: GeoGSplat uses a dual-branch encoder that builds Anchors for coarse 3D structure and a Triplane for fine-grained scene features. A hierarchical decoder then progressively decodes dense 3D points and Gaussian primitives for reconstruction and novel view synthesis.
rw2BeOY7qL.key_idea: Anchors and a triplane supply coarse and fine 3D structure, and a hierarchical decoder predicts dense 3D points before Gaussian primitives.
rw2BeOY7qL.evidence: Compared with pixel-aligned and non-pixel-aligned Gaussian splatting methods on DTU and NRGBD for novel view synthesis and reconstruction, with the gap reported to widen as target viewpoints move farther from the input cameras.

7F3kdZlfo9.one_liner: Multi-player video world model with player, group, and global tokens in attention and budget-constrained dynamic grouping by camera trajectory.
7F3kdZlfo9.problem: Fully-connected communication (e.g., Solaris) has quadratic attention cost in the number of players, and centralized approaches (e.g., γ-World) suffer interference between unrelated events in a shared global representation.
7F3kdZlfo9.method: Multics adds group tokens to self-attention that aggregate locally relevant player information and connect to global tokens for cross-group communication, with group-token parameters shared across group slots. Players are grouped dynamically from recent camera trajectories under a communication budget.
7F3kdZlfo9.key_idea: Route inter-player attention through group tokens with shared parameters, linked to global tokens, so unrelated local events do not mix directly.
7F3kdZlfo9.evidence: The visible abstract is cut off at the start of the experiments and names no datasets, baselines, or metrics.

WDxzxRDx8G.one_liner: On-policy self-distillation where a frozen teacher sees the most informative non-target-language context chosen per training instance.
WDxzxRDx8G.problem: Multilingual LLM knowledge is not equally accessible through every language, and the most informative language varies by question, domain, and culture, so fixed English supervision is suboptimal.
WDxzxRDx8G.method: A one-time offline probe measures how each candidate-language context changes the likelihood of the target-language reference answer and picks the most informative non-target language per instance. In training, the student sees only the target-language question and generates on-policy, while a frozen teacher also sees the selected crosslingual context and gives dense token-level supervision.
WDxzxRDx8G.key_idea: Choose the privileged-context language per instance by how much it raises the target-language reference answer's likelihood, and show it only to the frozen teacher.
WDxzxRDx8G.evidence: Experiments across multiple languages, model scales, and tasks against compared methods, plus ablations indicating that language selection helps beyond merely adding privileged context.

qPZcakh75D.one_liner: LLM agent for materials discovery that logs parent-edit-child transitions with property deltas and ranks edits by predicted constraint-violation reduction.
qPZcakh75D.problem: Existing materials-discovery LLM agents store evaluated candidates and scores but not which executable edits caused useful property changes, which makes local refinement hard when objectives compete.
qPZcakh75D.method: TRACE records each local refinement as a parent-edit-child transition with observed property deltas and aggregates this evidence into reusable edit-effect estimates. It ranks future edits by predicted ability to reduce the current candidate's remaining constraint violations without damaging objectives already satisfied.
qPZcakh75D.key_idea: Treat each evaluated parent-edit-child transition as feedback, estimate reusable edit effects from property deltas, and rank edits by predicted reduction of remaining constraint violations.
qPZcakh75D.evidence: A controlled same-backbone comparison against LLEMA, described as the state-of-the-art LLM-agent baseline; the abstract names no materials datasets or tasks.
qPZcakh75D.claimed_gains: Raises macro-average hit rate from 18.13% to 25.96% over LLEMA in a controlled same-backbone comparison.

nJBhZtemst.one_liner: Action-conditioned world model: PointFlow-coupled video generation bridges human-robot gap; GRPO on perturbed actions teaches failure dynamics.
nJBhZtemst.problem: Robot datasets cover few interaction dynamics, the embodiment gap blocks learning from egocentric human video, and mostly successful demonstrations leave failure dynamics underrepresented.
nJBhZtemst.method: HF-WM uses a dual-branch framework that couples video generation with auxiliary PointFlow prediction, using stabilized PointFlow as a unified human-robot motion representation that suppresses egocentric camera motion. It then post-trains with GRPO on perturbed actions derived from successful demonstrations, guided by action-alignment and physical-plausibility rewards.
nJBhZtemst.key_idea: Share stabilized PointFlow as the human-robot motion representation, and learn failures by GRPO on perturbed actions rewarded for action alignment and physical plausibility.
nJBhZtemst.evidence: The visible abstract is cut off before any experiments, so no datasets, baselines, or results are stated.

6E10PuDM2z.one_liner: An orchestrator decides per chunk whether to drop, keep or clean pretraining data, choosing operations and writing rewrite instructions.
6E10PuDM2z.problem: Existing pretraining data processing fixes one strategy at the corpus or domain level and applies it uniformly to many examples, without adapting to each example.
6E10PuDM2z.method: DataOrchestra unifies processing operations and has an orchestrator decide, for each chunk, to drop, leave untouched, or clean it. For cleaning it selects one or more downstream operations, from programmatic editing to LLM-based rewriting, and generates a concrete instruction that the corresponding tool model executes.
6E10PuDM2z.key_idea: An orchestrator picks drop, keep or clean per chunk, then selects operations and writes a concrete instruction for each rewriting tool model.
6E10PuDM2z.evidence: Models from 0.5B to 7B were pretrained from scratch on processed web data and evaluated on 11 benchmarks, plus math continued pretraining against stronger processing baselines.
6E10PuDM2z.claimed_gains: Stable average gains over individual data-processing methods across 11 benchmarks for 0.5B to 7B models, with gain magnitudes not stated.

oC2k9xA1mU.one_liner: Video text editing with a trajectory-aligned glyph rendering reference and depth-normalized recognizer-feature supervision, plus the VTEdit benchmark.
oC2k9xA1mU.problem: Video diffusion models produce garbled or wrong characters when editing text, especially complex-stroke characters, while the edited text must be correct in every frame and move coherently with the scene.
oC2k9xA1mU.method: They render a per-frame glyph reference that follows the text's position and perspective along its trajectory, and add supervision on multi-depth features of a frozen text recognizer using per-depth normalized errors. They also build VTEdit, a benchmark for text replacement and addition.
oC2k9xA1mU.key_idea: Render per-frame glyph references along the text trajectory and add a loss on depth-normalized frozen text-recognizer features targeting stroke errors.
oC2k9xA1mU.evidence: Experiments on VTEdit (288 real-scene clips with 440 annotated text trajectories) against image text editing methods, video editing methods, and commercial models, plus a user study.
oC2k9xA1mU.claimed_gains: Sentence accuracy of 0.9408 on VTEdit, with the highest preference in a user study.

GqKNRY7qN5.one_liner: Video VLM using two tokens per frame: Anchor Token for global context, Innovation Token for inter-frame changes.
GqKNRY7qN5.problem: Embodied and wearable systems need fast, low-cost video understanding, and it is unclear how much understanding survives when the per-frame visual-token budget is pushed to an extreme.
GqKNRY7qN5.method: GlanceVLM fixes a budget of two tokens per frame: an Anchor Token for global semantic context and an Innovation Token for temporally distinctive evidence. Difference-guided innovation encoding uses inter-frame changes to select informative regions while retaining their current-frame visual content.
GqKNRY7qN5.key_idea: Give each frame an anchor token for what is present and an innovation token built from regions selected by inter-frame differences.
GqKNRY7qN5.evidence: The visible abstract is cut off before the experiments, so no benchmarks, models, or results are stated.

K6YNRA19N4.one_liner: Proves row-wise normalization yields higher population accuracy than Adam and Muon in high-dimensional multiclass classification via class-wise geometry.
K6YNRA19N4.problem: Optimizers can fit the same training data yet select classifiers with different geometries, and it is unclear whether this provably changes population performance.
K6YNRA19N4.method: They analyze row-wise normalization against full-batch Adam (a proxy for random-reshuffling Adam) and exact-SVD Muon under an isotropic Gaussian-cloud data model. The analysis is then extended to full-batch training on class means with independently oriented class-mean and test-noise covariances, including power-law spectra.
K6YNRA19N4.key_idea: Row normalization's class-wise Euclidean geometry preserves population decision-boundary directions asymptotically, while Adam's coordinate-wise and Muon's spectral geometries distort them.
K6YNRA19N4.evidence: Theoretical results under the Gaussian-cloud model and several extensions, supported by synthetic and last-layer language-model experiments.

hvx3qG3rB6.one_liner: Self-evolving runtime for frozen VLM agents that distills CT-reading trajectories into evidence-grounded multimodal skills scored by an adoption-aware credit.
hvx3qG3rB6.problem: Memory-augmented 3D medical methods keep raw, noisy traces as text that loses spatial detail and lack adoption-aware estimates of memory utility, while other 3D medical methods depend on external teacher supervision.
hvx3qG3rB6.method: 3DMedEvo distills informative trajectories from frozen VLM agents reading CT scans into structured multimodal skills, combining reusable procedures with visual exemplars in a multi-branch repository, through outcome-guided reflection and without extra teacher supervision. An adoption-aware Skill Credit Score (SCS) calibrates skill reliability to guide retrieval and uncertainty-aware governance in a loop of skill acquisition, evaluation, and revision.
hvx3qG3rB6.key_idea: Score each distilled skill with an adoption-aware Skill Credit Score from observed utility, and use it to guide retrieval and revision of skills.
hvx3qG3rB6.evidence: Experiments on two established clinical benchmarks; the rest of the evaluation is cut off in the visible abstract.

pSJtPKzdPa.one_liner: Shows 3D LLMs ignore 3D positions; feeds the LLM only mask-selected tokens of question-named objects with their 3D positions.
pSJtPKzdPa.problem: 3D LLMs report gains from injected geometry, but it is unclear whether they use it; current benchmarks can be solved from appearance and language cues, and an autoregressive decoder is never forced to bind named entities to 3D locations.
pSJtPKzdPa.method: They permute or zero the 3D positions of visual tokens in five 3D LLMs and train MLP probes on hidden states. They then propose a model that detects and segments objects named in the question, picks one mask per name with a name-conditioned matcher, and passes only the covered patch tokens with their 3D positions to the LLM for metric reasoning.
pSJtPKzdPa.key_idea: Detect and segment objects named in the question, match one mask per name, and pass only mask-covered patch tokens with 3D positions to the LLM.
pSJtPKzdPa.evidence: Across five 3D LLMs, permuting or zeroing positions leaves performance essentially unchanged, and MLP probes recover relative 3D offsets from hidden states; the new model is trained on ScanQA, SQA3D, and R3D-Bench-style metric questions built on ScanNet.

Sv9XYgf01w.one_liner: Imputes missing history for frozen forecasters by solving a sparse quadratic program coupling local smoothness with cross-period reference increments.
Sv9XYgf01w.problem: Missing intervals in the history distort time series foundation model forecasts, and existing imputers minimize pointwise reconstruction error on the history without considering the effect on a frozen forecaster.
Sv9XYgf01w.method: SPImpute reconstructs missing intervals from observed history and a known period by solving a constrained sparse quadratic program that couples local smoothness with cross-period reference increments. For long gaps with same-phase donors on one side it adds a drift-corrected phase candidate, and candidate weights and phase replacement are chosen by self-supervised block masking on the observed history without querying the forecaster.
Sv9XYgf01w.key_idea: Solve a sparse quadratic program coupling local smoothness with cross-period reference increments, add drift-corrected donor levels for one-sided gaps, and pick weights by self-supervised masking.
Sv9XYgf01w.evidence: 19 series and five missing rates, comparing 21 imputers under the Sundial and TimesFM-2.5 forecasters.
Sv9XYgf01w.claimed_gains: Ranks first among 21 imputers under Sundial and TimesFM-2.5 (mean MSE ranks 5.39 and 6.38), with source-averaged relative MSE reductions of 10.81%, 10.11%, and 2.69% against baselines starting with Linear (the list is cut off in the abstract).

wG5BACjg5I.one_liner: Guides discrete diffusion by pairing a denoiser-marginal joint model with a compiled finite-state model of the sequence objective.
wG5BACjg5I.problem: Guiding discrete diffusion with a sequence-level objective is hard because an unresolved token's value depends on the other tokens it can form a high-reward sequence with, and enumerating completions grows exponentially with the number of unresolved positions.
wG5BACjg5I.method: At each diffusion step, a target-free carrier absorbs the denoiser's marginal token distributions into a joint model over unresolved tokens, while a compiled finite-state model records how token combinations affect the sequence-level preference. Pairing their states transfers global preferences to unresolved positions and samples a clean reconstruction without retraining, supporting hard constraints and learned soft objectives.
wG5BACjg5I.key_idea: Pair states of a carrier model built from denoiser marginals with a compiled finite-state model of the objective, avoiding enumeration of completions.
wG5BACjg5I.evidence: Evaluated on multiple symbolic, language, and biological benchmarks, with task-dependent quality and diversity trade-offs.

DfdVWSoauj.one_liner: Benchmark of 650 multi-user, multi-turn group travel-planning tasks in a group-chat sandbox with cached tool data for offline evaluation.
DfdVWSoauj.problem: Existing LLM travel-planning benchmarks reduce planning to a single user, sidestepping private-preference discovery, conflict surfacing and balancing utility against fairness.
DfdVWSoauj.method: Built from real user profiles, POI data and ticket prices, with 650 tasks across three difficulty levels run in a synchronous group-chat sandbox with cached tool data. It probes elicitation, coordination and planning using rule-based outcome metrics and LLM-judge process metrics.
DfdVWSoauj.key_idea: Test agents in a simulated group chat where private preferences must be elicited, conflicts resolved by compromise or subgrouping, and plans scored for utility and fairness.
DfdVWSoauj.evidence: Evaluation across a wide range of frontier models (the abstract is truncated before the results).

QP8cG6lCPB.one_liner: Zero Flux compares discrete distributions by checking whether local probability fluxes of a flow-matching model vanish at the midpoint.
QP8cG6lCPB.problem: Comparing high-dimensional discrete distributions is hard because the state space grows exponentially, and the flow-based criterion with a vanishing midpoint vector field does not naturally apply to discrete data.
QP8cG6lCPB.method: The flow-matching two-sample criterion is extended to discrete data: under independent coupling, all local probability fluxes vanish at the midpoint if and only if the two distributions are identical. The resulting discrepancy decomposes into local contributions and is estimated from samples, with finite-sample error bounds.
QP8cG6lCPB.key_idea: Use local probability fluxes of a discrete flow at the midpoint under independent coupling as a discrepancy that is zero if and only if the two distributions match.
QP8cG6lCPB.evidence: A proof of the if-and-only-if property, finite-sample error bounds for the estimator, and experiments on synthetic and real categorical data.

L4LO2bXgyT.one_liner: Video reward model that first generates query-adaptive rubrics, then scores with them, trained by two-stage Rubric-Guided Policy Optimization.
L4LO2bXgyT.problem: Video reward models that map subjective quality directly to one scalar produce unstable scores with scalar drift, making rewards unreliable for RL.
L4LO2bXgyT.method: RewardVerse inserts a dynamic rubric between the query and scorer; RGPO first warms up the scorer on self-evolving seed rubrics, then jointly optimizes the rubric generator for query-adaptive criteria while aligning the scorer with human ratings.
L4LO2bXgyT.key_idea: Generate explicit evaluation criteria first, then score against them, so rubrics act as a stable semantic anchor against scalar drift.
L4LO2bXgyT.evidence: Experiments on the 16-dimensional EvalVerse benchmark and external datasets; the rest is cut off in the abstract.

c0HwoO0emU.one_liner: Generates trial-level macaque V1, V4, and IT multi-unit activity with a conditional rectified flow and routed visual experts.
c0HwoO0emU.problem: Deterministic neural encoding models predict mean responses but do not capture trial-to-trial variability and joint population covariance across visual areas.
c0HwoO0emU.method: Image2MUA is a conditional rectified flow model trained from one response per training image. Population self-attention models coordinated trial variability, and factorized visual expert routing mixes visual representations per channel using channel preferences plus image-dependent adjustments.
c0HwoO0emU.key_idea: Condition a rectified flow on image features, with population self-attention for joint variability and factorized per-channel routing over visual experts.
c0HwoO0emU.evidence: Two macaques with V1, V4, and IT recordings, compared with deterministic regression, Gaussian outputs, and diffusion on the same visual and routing backbone.
c0HwoO0emU.claimed_gains: not stated (abstract reports improved mean prediction, marginal distribution fidelity, and average covariance without numbers)

zJlPojCmqs.one_liner: Trains a small LLM with RL to apply one Keep/Delete/Replace edit to retrieved in-context demonstrations.
zJlPojCmqs.problem: ICL quality depends heavily on the demonstration set, exhaustive search is combinatorial, and existing selectors use relevance or likelihood proxies and repeated, costly queries to the target LLM.
zJlPojCmqs.method: Local demonstration editing (LDE) frames selection as constrained local search from an initially retrieved set and reduces it to policy search. A small LLM, Jev-LDE, is trained with reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards to choose Keep, Delete, or Replace actions, and at test time makes one edit followed by one target-LLM inference.
zJlPojCmqs.key_idea: Train a small policy with verifiable-reward RL to make a single Keep, Delete, or Replace edit on a retrieved demonstration set, avoiding iterative scoring or subset search.
zJlPojCmqs.evidence: Standard classification benchmarks with various target LLMs using Jev-LDE as a plug-and-play module (the abstract is cut off before the results).

wTp5i5sUQ9.one_liner: World-model-guided loop that imagines skill failures, finds the first failing subtask, and directs demonstration collection and adapter updates.
wTp5i5sUQ9.problem: Improving long-horizon manipulation compositions with additional end-to-end demonstrations is costly, and a self-improving system must decide what to teach next and where to apply supervision.
wTp5i5sUQ9.method: RoboCoach's Route-Imagine-Diagnose-Improve (RIDI) loop runs reusable skill experts inside CoachWorld, a shared action-conditioned world model, and a progress judge records the first subtask that fails. Aggregated records select which subtask demonstrations to acquire and which expert adapters to update.
wTp5i5sUQ9.key_idea: Records the first failing subtask in imagined rollouts from a shared action-conditioned world model to choose which demonstrations to collect and which expert adapters to update.
wTp5i5sUQ9.evidence: Two simulation suites and two real-robot platforms (Franka and AgileX) with matched-budget baselines; imagined and deployed success are compared over 22 task-policy pairs.
wTp5i5sUQ9.claimed_gains: With 150 additional subtask demonstrations, success rises from 13.3% to 75.0% on Franka and from 40.0% to 83.8% on AgileX; coached experts reach 35.0% on four held-out compositions versus 0% for a shared-policy baseline; imagined and deployed success correlate at rho = 0.840.

83QM0tLiCR.one_liner: Empirical scaling study of how many times to repeat domain data in LLM pretraining mixtures at fixed tokens-per-parameter.
83QM0tLiCR.problem: As models and token budgets scale, scarce high-quality domain data is diluted in the mixture, and repeating it counteracts dilution but risks overfitting.
83QM0tLiCR.method: The paper studies the optimal repetition count for fixed domains while the training-token budget grows proportionally with model size, and compares optimal repetition across domains against final validation loss and unique data amount.
83QM0tLiCR.key_idea: Tune domain repetition counts on small proxy models at the same tokens-per-parameter, since optimal repetition rises mildly with model size and tracks domain validation loss.
83QM0tLiCR.evidence: Controlled pretraining experiments across model sizes and several domains at fixed tokens-per-parameter; model sizes and domains are not stated in the abstract.
83QM0tLiCR.claimed_gains: not stated; findings are qualitative: optimal repetition count mildly increases with model size and is strongly negatively correlated with a domain's final validation loss.

DBRgxcPpEM.one_liner: Flow-matching motion generator conditioned on a shared canvas of position and rotation cues across joints and time, with cue imputation.
DBRgxcPpEM.problem: Character animation needs natural motion plus precise, versatile control from heterogeneous kinematic cues (timing, motion range, routes) that may be dense or sparse, full or partial.
DBRgxcPpEM.method: AnimateCanvas represents kinematic cues on a motion canvas of position and rotation values across body joints and time, and a shared flow-matching model generates motion conditioned on it, with optional language and input motion. Cue imputation holds specified values fixed in training and sampling, and a compositional cue sampler varies cue timing, channels, and combinations.
DBRgxcPpEM.key_idea: Specified cues are clamped on a joint-by-time canvas during both training and sampling, so one flow-matching generator completes arbitrary cue subsets into full-body motion.
DBRgxcPpEM.evidence: The abstract is cut off before the evaluation, so datasets and baselines are not visible.

1H0upSezMg.one_liner: Hierarchical generator for irregular multivariate time series that models raw sample points at sample, window, and point levels.
1H0upSezMg.problem: Existing generators regularize irregular observations, bin them into fixed time bins, or use one smooth continuous-time state, which alters the sampling process and loses irregular sampling rhythms and asynchronous variable interactions.
1H0upSezMg.method: HiGen directly models the original sample points and organizes generation at sample, window, and point levels. Real time intervals at window and point level model temporal dynamics, and all three levels model variable interactions.
1H0upSezMg.key_idea: Generates in three nested levels (sample, window, point) using real time intervals, preserving irregular sampling rhythms and asynchronous variable relationships.
1H0upSezMg.evidence: Experiments on irregular multivariate time series datasets (not named in the abstract) comparing downstream utility and generation fidelity against baselines.
1H0upSezMg.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract claims better downstream utility and generation fidelity than baselines without numbers.

zx3mLwGgKx.one_liner: Adapts frozen tile embeddings for slide classification with a single learnable query that exponentially tilts the instance distribution.
zx3mLwGgKx.problem: Downstream multiple-instance learning for whole-slide images is usually adapted with a fully trainable attention network or transformer, which raises the question of how much task-specific adaptation strong frozen encoders actually need.
zx3mLwGgKx.method: With a frozen tile encoder, one learnable d-dimensional query exponentially tilts the empirical distribution of tile embeddings, forms a weighted expectation, and passes it to a linear classifier. They show this solves an entropy-regularized instance-selection problem whose temperature interpolates between mean pooling and hard instance selection.
zx3mLwGgKx.key_idea: Single-query exponential tilting of frozen tile embeddings solves entropy-regularized instance selection, with temperature interpolating between mean pooling and hard selection.
zx3mLwGgKx.evidence: A provisional result scaffold on fine-grained EBRAINS and few-shot settings, plus theory showing the representation Jacobian is a tile-feature covariance operator.
zx3mLwGgKx.claimed_gains: The one-query adaptation is within one percentage point of a substantially richer full-data aggregator on fine-grained EBRAINS, with a larger advantage in few-shot settings (the abstract is cut off).

K5M5RDK2zj.one_liner: ReliLogic tests LLM logical reasoning with equivalent-form and intervention variants of propositional entailment questions, scoring reliability beyond accuracy.
K5M5RDK2zj.problem: High accuracy on logical reasoning benchmarks does not show that a model reliably identifies and responds to the underlying logical relations.
K5M5RDK2zj.method: ReliLogic is a behavioral reliability framework over propositional-logic entailment questions, with a Representation Set of four logically equivalent forms and an Intervention Set of logic-preserving and logic-altering interventions. It measures cross-representation reliability, selective logical responsiveness, and instance-level prediction stability.
K5M5RDK2zj.key_idea: Pose the same entailment under four equivalent representations and under logic-preserving versus logic-altering interventions, then score consistency and responsiveness instead of accuracy alone.
K5M5RDK2zj.evidence: Evaluations across 74 language-model configurations that reveal failure modes not reflected by accuracy.

8F0H5aq24A.one_liner: Embeds a compact, spatially shuffled source latent in an image so a receiver can localize manipulations and recover overwritten content.
8F0H5aq24A.problem: Passive localization cannot recover source content that is no longer present, and existing self-recovery methods couple payload construction and spatial dispersion at image resolution.
8F0H5aq24A.method: SHIM embeds a compact, spatially shuffled source latent; the receiver decodes it in two orders, direct decoding (retains manipulation-related inconsistencies) and inverse-shuffle decoding (restores source alignment). A locator combines both views with the received image, and a mask-guided refiner corrects the aligned estimate within the predicted repair support.
8F0H5aq24A.key_idea: Decode one embedded, shuffled latent in two orders and let a locator combine the inconsistent direct view with the source-aligned inverse-shuffle view.
8F0H5aq24A.evidence: valAGE-Set for localization and recovery after channel degradation, plus a separate evaluation on COCO, ImageNet, and CelebA-HQ against Imuge+ and ReImage, with controlled analyses of view complementarity and refinement.
8F0H5aq24A.claimed_gains: Stronger dataset-averaged recovery than Imuge+ and ReImage across diverse channel conditions on COCO, ImageNet, and CelebA-HQ; no numeric gains are visible in the abstract.

TpH1ShGLYr.one_liner: Survey-based audit contrasting worker desire with AI-expert capability ratings across tasks using a five-level Human Agency Scale.
TpH1ShGLYr.problem: Agent benchmarks and exposure studies measure what agents can do but cannot separate technical feasibility from social acceptability and worker preferences, leaving open which tasks to automate and which to augment.
TpH1ShGLYr.method: A task-level auditing framework introduces the Human Agency Scale (H1-H5) as a shared evaluation language. WORKBank instantiates it with data from 1,500 domain workers across 104 occupations and capability assessments from 52 AI experts.
TpH1ShGLYr.key_idea: Measure worker desire and AI capability on the same tasks with a shared five-level Human Agency Scale to expose desire-capability mismatches.
TpH1ShGLYr.evidence: Survey data from 1,500 workers across 104 occupations and 52 AI experts, demonstrated in three use cases (auditing automation demand across sectors, mismatches with AI research and investment, and informing collaborative design).
TpH1ShGLYr.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports resource scale: 1,500 workers, 104 occupations, 52 AI experts)

1PRRCTyjwN.one_liner: Analyzes why score-function gradient estimators need many queries under discrete evaluators: boundary starvation and tangential noise.
1PRRCTyjwN.problem: Unbiased score-function gradient estimators for discrete downstream evaluators can require many evaluations before becoming informative.
1PRRCTyjwN.method: They study boundary starvation, which limits the appearance of distinct feedback, and tangential noise, which adds variance in directions that do not change the loss. In a binary planar model they derive exact activation probabilities, gradient covariances, and complete-group budgets, then link estimation to optimization by showing removal of tangential noise leaves SGD objective trajectories unchanged while norm clipping couples it to the update.
1PRRCTyjwN.key_idea: Query cost splits into feedback activation (boundary starvation) and variance in loss-irrelevant tangential directions, which can be separated analytically.
1PRRCTyjwN.evidence: Exact derivations in a binary planar model, a rare-feedback analysis, a fixed-subspace variance identity for multivalued feedback, and numerical experiments.
1PRRCTyjwN.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract presents theoretical mechanism results supported by numerical experiments, without numbers)

PzlJfjWklS.one_liner: Compiles a dataset-specific forward-inverse CAE optimizer using an LLM tuned by rule-residual preference optimization on counterfactual build sweeps.
PzlJfjWklS.problem: Applying learned physics surrogates to inverse design on a new dataset needs a hand-built pipeline and dozens of expert decisions, and proprietary CAE data cannot be pooled for one large model.
PzlJfjWklS.method: From a raw CAE dataset, emits a deployable optimizer that predicts physical fields and reshapes geometry through them. Counterfactual build sweeps turn fifteen datasets into hundreds of process-rewarded preference pairs, confirmed lessons harden into rules and precedents, and RRPO tunes the language model only on decisions no rule answers.
PzlJfjWklS.key_idea: Learn build expertise from counterfactual retraining sweeps as preference pairs, harden confirmed lessons into rules, and tune the LLM only where rules give no answer.
PzlJfjWklS.evidence: Fifteen datasets from four physics domains, with evaluation on frozen decision boards against frontier models.
PzlJfjWklS.claimed_gains: On frozen decision boards it answers every regime probe that frontier models miss and cuts the decision loss from 22.4 R2 points to 0.1.

ZyHzck8bli.one_liner: IDOL decodes planning-relevant motion deltas from adjacent predicted latent BEV futures using inverse dynamics to refine trajectory queries.
ZyHzck8bli.problem: Future prediction in world-model-based end-to-end driving does not improve planning unless predicted scene evolution is converted into trajectory updates, and existing methods forecast futures without decoding the motion implications of state transitions.
ZyHzck8bli.method: A BEV world model predicts multiple future latent scene states, and an inverse dynamics model applied to adjacent latent futures decodes transition-aware trajectory features and motion deltas. These features refine candidate-specific planning queries through spatial cross-attention and global modulation.
ZyHzck8bli.key_idea: Apply inverse dynamics to adjacent latent BEV futures to recover motion deltas that refine candidate planning queries, linking future prediction to trajectory optimization.

KDYa6p183y.one_liner: Proves when reevaluating noisy fitness in NSGA-II hurts or helps, using LOTZ and a PairedCOCZ benchmark under one-bit noise.
KDYa6p183y.problem: It is unclear whether NSGA-II under noisy evaluations should reevaluate solutions every generation or retain their initial noisy fitness values.
KDYa6p183y.method: A runtime analysis of NSGA-II under one-bit prior noise on LOTZ and on a constructed benchmark, PairedCOCZ, comparing retained initial fitness with reevaluation while all other algorithm settings stay unchanged.
KDYa6p183y.key_idea: Compare expected runtime when initial noisy fitness is kept versus reevaluated each generation, where the effect of reevaluation flips with benchmark and noise level.
KDYa6p183y.evidence: Theoretical runtime proofs on LOTZ (noise between omega(sqrt(log n / n)) and O(1/log n)) and on PairedCOCZ (noise below but sufficiently close to one); no experiments are stated.
KDYa6p183y.claimed_gains: On LOTZ, retaining initial fitness gives polynomial expected runtime while reevaluation is superpolynomial; on PairedCOCZ, reevaluation gives polynomial runtime versus at least exponential without it.

qgHKjD7D3W.one_liner: Doubly robust estimator separating peer effects through positive and negative network ties using sign-specific outcome models.
qgHKjD7D3W.problem: Counting treated neighbors without distinguishing supportive and antagonistic ties can hide opposing influences when evaluating network interventions.
qgHKjD7D3W.method: Defines effects through positive ties, negative ties, their interaction and a sign-composition effect, and gives identification formulas. SiDE combines sign-specific outcome models with exposure probabilities induced by individual treatment assignment, with approximate intervals that account for overlapping neighborhoods.
qgHKjD7D3W.key_idea: Exposure is split by tie sign, and a doubly robust score combines sign-specific outcome models with exposure probabilities induced by individual treatment assignment.
qgHKjD7D3W.evidence: A double-robustness proof for the score, semi-synthetic experiments on six real signed networks, and an exploratory reanalysis of published school-experiment data.
qgHKjD7D3W.claimed_gains: The reanalysis gives a positive estimate of the spend-time-tie peer effect on wristband wearing, but the intervals for all four effects include zero after multiple-comparison adjustment.

sXbeNXFVhg.one_liner: Visuo-tactile video world model on a shared multimodal canvas, post-trained with scene, modality and state reward models.
sXbeNXFVhg.problem: Visually plausible world-model predictions can misrepresent contact dynamics and task outcomes, giving unreliable feedback for robot policy evaluation and learning.
sXbeNXFVhg.method: PhysCanvas organizes multi-view RGB, tactile images, marker displacement and task state into one canvas sharing a video VAE and pretrained generative backbone, with motion images from forward kinematics for action conditioning. Consistency-aware post-training uses frozen Scene, Modality and State Reward Models, and the model supports closed-loop policy evaluation and imagined interactions and rewards for GRPO updates.
sXbeNXFVhg.key_idea: Tactile signals are rendered as images sharing a video VAE and backbone with RGB, and three frozen reward models enforce scene preservation, visual-tactile compatibility and task-outcome agreement.
sXbeNXFVhg.evidence: Four real-world manipulation tasks, measuring the effect of State Reward Model supervision on task-wise Pearson correlations.

T370Kff8xJ.one_liner: Estimates correctness of parametric-knowledge and context-based answers from frozen LLM hidden states to trust either source or abstain.
T370Kff8xJ.problem: When retrieved context and parametric knowledge conflict or both fail, existing RAG approaches coordinate which source to use without asking whether each answer path is correct.
T370Kff8xJ.method: Builds a model-specific, ground-truth-aligned conflict benchmark (about 69K query-context instances per backbone from five conflict-QA datasets), then SABER extracts a self-prior and source-conditioned reasoning representations from frozen hidden states. Two lightweight predictors estimate PK-side and CK-side correctness beliefs, mapped to a 4-cell decision: trust PK, trust CK, trust both, or abstain.
T370Kff8xJ.key_idea: Two lightweight predictors on frozen hidden states estimate belief that the parametric answer and the context-based answer are each correct, then map the pair to a four-way decision.
T370Kff8xJ.evidence: Four LLM backbones and five datasets against ten baselines, with risk-coverage curves when configured to abstain.
T370Kff8xJ.claimed_gains: Improves end-to-end accuracy and conflict-specific faithfulness over ten baselines, with the largest gains on conflict-heavy datasets; no numbers are stated in the abstract.

Inwyz6n5KE.one_liner: Theorem-driven symbolic generator of solid-geometry problems with aligned diagrams and verifiable reasoning traces for MLLM training and evaluation.
Inwyz6n5KE.problem: High-quality solid-geometry data with aligned diagrams and verifiable solutions is scarce, and existing generators focus on plane geometry.
Inwyz6n5KE.method: SolidGeoGen generates diverse problems with aligned diagrams, formal representations and verifiable reasoning traces, yielding S2Bench (2,000 problems, ten tasks) and S2Train (10,000 examples). VISTA, a visual-structure-informed and symbolic-trace-assisted training framework, is trained on S2Train.
Inwyz6n5KE.key_idea: Theorem-driven symbolic generation yields diagrams, formal representations and step-level verifiable traces from the same source, enabling process supervision.
Inwyz6n5KE.evidence: Evaluation of open-source and proprietary MLLMs on S2Bench, and training with VISTA on S2Train.
Inwyz6n5KE.claimed_gains: All evaluated open-source MLLMs score below 30% average accuracy on S2Bench and the strongest proprietary model reaches 67.2%; VISTA's gains are cut off in the abstract.

Fwc9p8VlfU.one_liner: Benchmark with fixation-based saliency gaps testing whether MLLMs use correctly localized evidence against distractors, plus activation patching.
Fwc9p8VlfU.problem: The ability of MLLMs to exploit correctly localized evidence against more salient distractors is largely unexplored.
Fwc9p8VlfU.method: DECOY has 2,163 images from four eye-tracking datasets and 9,596 human-written QA pairs across five task types, each graded by saliency gap; separate scores for Saliency Grounding, Target Grounding, and Answer Accuracy isolate suppression failures, and activation patching compares decodable information with its depth-dependent causal contribution.
Fwc9p8VlfU.key_idea: Grade each question by a fixation-based saliency gap, score grounding and answering separately, then use activation patching to contrast decodable target information with its causal effect by depth.
Fwc9p8VlfU.evidence: 24 MLLMs evaluated; restricting the input to target evidence helps more than indicating its location, and answer-relevant information stays decodable while patching efficacy changes with depth (abstract truncated).
Fwc9p8VlfU.claimed_gains: Lowest rate of distractor-linked answers after correct grounding is 16.9% for models versus 1.9% for humans, and answering errors increase monotonically with the saliency gap.

9XBWRdb0nR.one_liner: Self-teaching post-training for unified multimodal models: splits interleaved rollouts into text and image chains, builds targets by reliability.
9XBWRdb0nR.problem: Existing UMM post-training either uses understanding as a fixed teacher to improve generation or relies on ground-truth trajectories to supervise both understanding and generation.
9XBWRdb0nR.method: Prism decouples a self-generated interleaved trajectory into a text chain and an image chain, assesses the reliability of each, and constructs a training target from their reliability states, with no ground-truth trajectories or external verifier.
9XBWRdb0nR.key_idea: Derive bidirectional supervision from self-generated interleaved rollouts by scoring text and image chains separately and choosing training targets from their reliability states.
9XBWRdb0nR.evidence: Experiments on SenseNova-U1 and BAGEL, evaluated with GenEval, DPG, MME, and MMVP.
9XBWRdb0nR.claimed_gains: On SenseNova-U1, GenEval improves from 85.8 to 89.2 (+3.4), DPG from 86.1 to 87.3 (+1.2), total MME from 2282.6 to 2311.6, and MMVP from 58.0 to 62.0.

geLz0x5TNO.one_liner: Video world model for egocentric navigation and manipulation, rendering head-trajectory and hand-mesh controls in one shared image space.
geLz0x5TNO.problem: Action-conditioned video world models typically handle either navigation or local manipulation, leaving their combination poorly supported.
geLz0x5TNO.method: Scene geometry reconstructed from the initial image is reprojected along the head trajectory and hand meshes are overlaid in prescribed poses, giving a visual condition that reuses the pretrained model's native visual-conditioning path; autoregressive generation supports long horizons.
geLz0x5TNO.key_idea: Express head and hand action conditions as one visual condition in image space (reprojected geometry plus rendered hand mesh), so no action-specific input modules are needed.
geLz0x5TNO.evidence: A curated unified dataset and a four-track benchmark with 846 test cases spanning navigation, manipulation, mobile manipulation, and long-horizon generation.
geLz0x5TNO.claimed_gains: Outperforms previous methods by a large margin across visual quality and (abstract truncated); no numbers stated.

vO20LdmZxT.one_liner: Trains a reference-free implicitness score for image-text pairs and uses it to stratify existing datasets into graded implicitness levels.
vO20LdmZxT.problem: Existing benchmarks describe implicitness through phenomenon-specific categories or binary labels, not by how indirectly an image-text pair conveys its meaning.
vO20LdmZxT.method: MM-ImpScore is trained on controlled semantic families that vary communicative directness, and measures the discrepancy between surface compositional meaning and pragmatic joint meaning; MM-ImpBench scores samples from six existing datasets and stratifies them into implicitness levels.
vO20LdmZxT.key_idea: Measure implicitness as the gap between an image-text pair's surface compositional meaning and its pragmatic joint meaning, learned from controlled semantic families.
vO20LdmZxT.evidence: Six existing datasets spanning hate speech, offensive content, sarcasm, and multimodal safety; evaluation of vision-language detectors across implicitness levels (abstract truncated).

xZYoMDqtv5.one_liner: Transfers text-to-image rewards to image-editing RL by mapping editing dimensions into the T2I reward space in two stages.
xZYoMDqtv5.problem: Editing-specific rewards are underdeveloped because they need costly instruction, source, and edited-image triplet supervision and task-dependent calibration, while T2I rewards are mature.
xZYoMDqtv5.method: Lever-Edit is a two-stage reward-transfer framework; Stage 1 learns a textual component (cut off in the abstract) to address the mismatch between relative edit instructions and the self-contained descriptions T2I rewards need. Quality transfers directly and reference consistency is converted by encoding the source content to preserve.
xZYoMDqtv5.key_idea: Map editing dimensions into T2I reward space: image quality directly, prompt following via a description of the desired visual state, reference consistency via encoding source content to preserve.
xZYoMDqtv5.evidence: The visible abstract is cut off before the experiments; not stated.

TNnhksIM7B.one_liner: Benchmark and automatically synthesized dialogue dataset for culturally diverse, low-resource music understanding in audio-language models.
TNnhksIM7B.problem: LALMs degrade on diverse global and low-resource folk music because of data imbalance and the lack of dedicated evaluation protocols.
TNnhksIM7B.method: UniVerseBench has 5,042 expert-curated Q&A pairs across 38 cultural entities, and UniVerseSet is an automated multi-turn dialogue dataset for multimodal alignment; the study compares multimodal imbalance learning strategies on Dense and Mixture-of-Experts LALMs, including latent representation alignment.
TNnhksIM7B.key_idea: Combine automated multi-turn dialogue curation with latent representation alignment to counter multimodal data imbalance for low-resource musical traditions.
TNnhksIM7B.evidence: Systematic study across Dense and MoE LALM architectures on UniVerseBench (abstract truncated).
TNnhksIM7B.claimed_gains: Automated curation with latent representation alignment yields significant gains on dense backbones (+14.9 pp); the MoE result is cut off in the abstract.

H9z6rvfCqA.one_liner: Jointly compresses 3D-scene visual tokens before the LLM and distills adaptively weighted multi-teacher vision priors during fine-tuning.
H9z6rvfCqA.problem: Video-based 3D multimodal LLMs incur heavy inference costs from dense multi-view visual tokens, while post-hoc token pruning sacrifices spatial reasoning accuracy.
H9z6rvfCqA.method: SAVR compresses multi-view visual tokens to a target budget prior to LLM ingestion within a single-stage 3D fine-tuning pipeline. To retain spatial cues under compression, it distills features from multiple vision foundation models into final-layer LLM visual representations using learnable adaptive teacher weights.
H9z6rvfCqA.key_idea: Couple pre-LLM visual token compression with adaptively weighted multi-teacher foundation-model distillation at the final LLM layer during 3D task fine-tuning.

XelnGzgYgI.one_liner: Stabilizes subgoal switching in hierarchical LLM agents by penalizing premature replanning and stale persistence in boundary updates.
XelnGzgYgI.problem: Learned subgoal boundary policies in hierarchical language agents often degenerate into every-turn replanning or prolonged retention of obsolete subgoals.
XelnGzgYgI.method: STAC applies constraint costs for premature replanning and stale subgoal persistence exclusively to the subgoal-boundary policy update while leaving task rewards and execution objectives unchanged. It offers a duration-based deterministic variant (STAC-D) and a probabilistic variant (STAC-P) that derives state-dependent boundary costs from learned semantic subgoal completion probabilities.
XelnGzgYgI.key_idea: Constrain hierarchical subgoal boundary updates with deterministic duration proxies or learned semantic-completion costs without altering primitive action rewards.
XelnGzgYgI.evidence: Evaluated with Qwen3-0.6B on interactive agent benchmarks including ALFWorld.
XelnGzgYgI.claimed_gains: With Qwen3-0.6B, STAC-P achieves 95.3% task success on ALFWorld and 74.2% on a second benchmark whose name is truncated in the abstract.

ZwOoQcLotV.one_liner: Integrates mobile agents into Android's native event, capability, and permission interfaces to manage concurrent dynamic tasks.
ZwOoQcLotV.problem: Pure GUI mobile agents lack operating-system event subscriptions and native cross-app execution channels needed to coordinate multiple ongoing tasks as device state and user plans evolve.
ZwOoQcLotV.method: The authors build Android OS-native agents that subscribe to live system and app state changes, route events to corresponding active tasks, and execute actions through permission-checked native OS interfaces. They also introduce DynamicWorld, a benchmark of concurrent multi-app tasks under evolving device states and user revisions.
ZwOoQcLotV.key_idea: Hook agents directly into mobile OS event streams, task routing, and permission-governed native interfaces instead of relying solely on screen-level GUI polling.
ZwOoQcLotV.evidence: Implemented on Android and evaluated over three runs with GPT-5.4 against the MobileClaw GUI agent on the DynamicWorld benchmark.
